On-Chain Operator. Lesson 8.4, The operating playbook: deploy, monitor, respond, review. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You can already pull a number off a chain. The operating system is what you do with it: a register, a journal, and a kill rule.
Deploy: due diligence done · before-signing checklist · test amount · journal row (protocol, chain, contracts, amount, entry, thesis, kill rules, approvals).
Monitor: daily HF/pegs/ranges/incidents; weekly P&L vs benchmark, harvest, revoke; monthly register review.
Respond: pre-written actions for each trigger (see Module 11.5 for incidents).
Review: net return after all costs vs benchmark; simplify anything you can't explain in one sentence.

Check yourself. 1. The four phases? The answer: Deploy, monitor, respond, review.
Check yourself. 2. What goes in a journal row? The answer: Position, amount, date, thesis, kill rules, approvals and ongoing results.
Check yourself. 3. What to do with a strategy you can't explain simply? The answer: Simplify it or exit.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to run every position through the same four-phase routine.
First, Deploy: due diligence done times before-signing checklist times test amount times journal row (protocol, chain, contracts, amount, entry, thesis, kill rules, approvals).
Next, Monitor: daily health factor/pegs/ranges/incidents; weekly P and L versus benchmark, harvest, revoke; monthly register review.
Then, Respond: pre-written actions for each trigger (see Module 11.5 for incidents).
And finally, Review: net return after all costs versus benchmark; simplify anything you can't explain in one sentence.
Amount or date: $10,000 times 2026-09-01.
Kill rules: Utilisation > 95% for 48h; oracle or collateral change; any incident.
